chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prays while sitting. He said: 'If you intend to pray while sitting and have the prayer of the standing person recorded for you, then recite while sitting. When you are at the end of the chapter, stand up, complete it, and bow; that will be recorded for you as the prayer of the standing person.'

And we have clarified that whoever prays the voluntary prayers while sitting despite being able to stand, prays two rak'ahs as one rak'ah, and this is preferable. If he makes one rak'ah in place of one, there is no blame upon him.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ بِرَكْعَةٍ: Two rak'ahs counted as one (half reward)
key_terms.صَلاَةُ اَلْقَائِمِ: The prayer of the standing person (full reward)
key_terms.لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ حَرَجٌ: There is no blame/difficulty upon him

ai.seo_question: How should one pray while sitting to receive the full reward of standing, and what is the ruling for voluntary prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanics of 'Salat al-Jalis' (praying while seated) to ensure the full reward of standing is attained, particularly by delaying the rise until the final verses of the Surah. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights the preference for maintaining the posture of standing even in voluntary prayers when capable, while acknowledging the flexibility in counting rak'ahs to avoid hardship.
